prompt: There is a bug report in ISSUE.md. Fix the code in this folder so the issue is resolved. Do not ask questions; make the fix.
final_response:
The fix is complete.

## What was wrong

The original `LRUCache`:
- `get` never updated recency, so it didn't record that `a` was most recently used.
- `put` always appended to `order`, even when the key already existed, so updating a key left a stale duplicate in the order and made `len(order)` grow — effectively counting updates against capacity and evicting the wrong item.

## The fix

In `cache.py`:

- `get` now moves a found key to the end of `order` (marking it most-recently-used) before returning it.
- `put` now removes an existing key from `order` before re-appending it, so an update refreshes recency without adding a duplicate or counting against capacity.

I verified the reported scenario and two related cases all pass:

- `put(a)`, `put(b)`, `get(a)`, `put(c)` (capacity 2) → `b` is evicted, `a` survives. ✅
- Updating an existing key no longer causes eviction. ✅
- `get` of a missing key still returns the `default`. ✅
